queries: SWE bench Pro September 2025 software engineering agents benchmark reliability

sources_considered.why: The original September 2025 version reports reproducible repository-level engineering evaluations.
Published later but explicitly reports August 2025 observations, within the target period.
A later methodological examination identifies weaknesses in SWE-Bench Pro. Used as context limiting confidence, not as a measurement of September 2025 model performance.
Read directly. Its controlled context-length tests concern retrieval and related tasks, not the claimed codebase-maintenance outcome.
The benchmark announcement offers less direct evidence than the original evaluation paper.

evidence_items.explanation: Agents successfully resolved a subset of repository-level maintenance and feature tasks under executable tests, contradicting literal inability to perform engineering tasks. The low success rates do not demonstrate reliable whole-job autonomy.

The August survey supports the narrower concern that dependable delegation remained limited and human supervision mattered. It does not support categorical inability, inability to adapt, or an inherent permanent barrier.

evidence_items.publisher: SWE-Bench Pro Verified authors via arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, following discussion of leakage and task-quality issues
evidence_items.explanation: The later analysis identifies leakage and task-quality problems in the benchmark. It limits confidence in interpreting reported scores, without supplying a corrected measurement of the particular September 2025 evaluations.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not establish that observed unreliability is an inherent, unavoidable property preventing software engineering.
The categorical learning and adaptation assertions are not separately settled.
No admitted controlled codebase-size experiment establishes the claimed general relationship between increasing code, variables, and failure.
The later benchmark critique does not quantify corrections to the specific original scores.
